data.gender_notes: Henricus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name 'Henricus', which means 'ruler of the house'. This name was popular among the Germanic and Roman populations, and was borne by several influential historical figures, including the Holy Roman Emperor Henry II and the English monarch Henry V. The name Henricus carries the meaning “Rule of the house” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Henricus usually hope their child will grow to embody rule of the house and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Henricus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rule of the house.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Henricus total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Henricus' has been associated with power, leadership, and royalty for centuries. Many Christian rulers in Europe, particularly in Germany and England, have borne this name throughout history. They were not only political leaders, but also considered as spiritual guides and protectors of their people, imparting a sense of strength and stability that resonates even today..
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Henricus' encapsulates the idea of being a protector, provider, and leader for one's family and spiritual community. It carries the spiritual connotation of living as a steward of one's household and responsibilities, embodying the virtues of love, loyalty, and courage in all aspects of life. This Christian name continues to inspire individuals to uphold the values of leadership, wisdom, and spiritual depth.
